doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Identity without an audience and Baron's difficult childhood
summary: Baron says he defined himself by audience energy, mentions an unsupportive childhood, and the good place he had reached before the pandemic.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well just to wrap up, this is a funny question about how you feel about yourself. We have, so used to playing gigs, that’s what we do. And being in front of people. And that’s what we do. And now we can’t do it.

That’s the premium question. It’s not a funny question, it’s a great question. Because working on myself is something I’ve been doing much of my adult life, changing who I believe I am. And it’s given me pause to look at, wow, a lot of — I don’t want to say self- esteem but I’m used to adulation. I’m used to the thing where I play for someone, ten people, a thousand people, two hundred, it doesn’t matter. And this energy — not even the words, “Oh you sounded great,” but the energy back and forth between us, I realized that I define myself from that. And it’s like it’s not the total definition but it’s a good part. And I’ll be honest with you and say something that you may not know — it’s been an issue. I did not have an easy childhood of support. And I rebelled against it. And I’ve had to work much of my adult life to feel good about what I do and I’ve really reached a great place on it. As a matter of fact, coming home from that radio show I felt man, all this was worth it. I feel so good, what I do, I’m one of these elders and sitting there with Bill Crow and Purdie, and I was telling them I was saying all of those youngsters and me you know, almost an oldster, really appreciate you guys. And Bill Crow said, “Well you’re an up- and-coming oldster yourself.” Something like that. And I really realized like for so many years I’ve been accepted and it’s coming in like gangbusters now. And so it’s like God damn I feel so good about myself and this, and then the pandemic comes. You know? So it’s taken some work you know. And I know I just exposed myself, because most people don’t have a clue about that. “Oh you’re great, you get up there and you take care of business” you do this, you do that. Yeah. And they’re right. So it’s a heavy time right now. I think a lot of people are working internally on themselves now.
